title: Political Ad Rates 2026: TV & CTV Costs by Market Size

facts.fact: AdImpact projects record political ad spending of $10.8 billion for the 2026 cycle (third-party projection cited by the vendor).
facts.quote: The 2026 cycle will see record political ad spending of $10.8 billion according to AdImpact projections.

facts.fact: The page's worked CPM example gives a cost of $2,500 for reaching 100,000 viewers at a $25 CPM.
facts.quote: Example: To reach 100,000 viewers at $25 CPM: Cost = (100,000 / 1,000) × $25 = $2,500

facts.fact: The page's worked CPP example gives a cost of $100,000 for 200 GRPs at a $500 cost per point.
facts.quote: Example: To achieve 200 GRPs at $500 CPP: Cost = 200 × $500 = $100,000

facts.fact: The vendor lists broadcast TV minimum commitments at roughly $5,000 to $50,000+.
The vendor lists cable TV minimum commitments at roughly $2,000 to $15,000+.
The vendor lists premium CTV minimum commitments at $10,000 to $50,000.
The vendor states self-serve CTV can have minimums as low as $50 to $100.
In the top 10 DMAs, the vendor lists a 30-second prime time (8-11 PM) spot at $15,000 to $75,000.
In mid-size markets (DMAs 11-50), the vendor lists a 30-second prime time spot at $2,000 to $10,000.
In small markets (DMAs 51+), the vendor lists a 30-second prime time spot at $200 to $2,000.
Under Section 315(b) lowest unit rate rules, the window runs 45 days before a primary election.
facts.quote: In the 45 days before a primary and the 60 days before a general or special election

facts.fact: The vendor states federal candidate ads must show the candidate's clear image plus a printed statement together for at least 4 seconds at the end of the ad.
facts.quote: shown together for at least 4 seconds at the end, saying the candidate approved the ad and their committee paid for it.

facts.fact: The vendor states zone buying adds 10-25% to base cable rates.
facts.quote: Zone buying adds 10-25% to base rates but reduces waste for district-specific races.

facts.fact: The vendor lists national news cable networks (CNN, Fox News, MSNBC) at a CPM of $20 to $40.
The vendor lists sports cable networks at a CPM of $25 to $50.
The vendor lists entertainment cable networks at a CPM of $10 to $25.
The vendor lists full-system local cable buys at a CPM of $5 to $15.
The vendor lists Hulu at a CPM of $30 to $45 with a direct minimum commitment of $20,000 to $50,000.
The vendor lists Peacock at a CPM of $25 to $40 with a minimum commitment of $15,000 to $40,000.
The vendor lists Paramount+ at a CPM of $25 to $40 with a minimum commitment of $15,000 to $35,000.
The vendor lists Disney+ (ad-supported) at a CPM of $35 to $50 with a minimum commitment of $25,000 or more.
The vendor lists Max (HBO) at a CPM of $30 to $50.
The vendor lists Tubi at a CPM of $12 to $22.
The vendor lists Roku Channel at a CPM of $15 to $25.
Adwave's page lists self-serve CTV political advertising CPMs at $20-35.
facts.quote: **Self-serve CTV rates:** * CPM: $20-35 * Media budgets from $30/day * No agency fees or markups

facts.fact: Adwave's page states that self-serve CTV media budgets start from $30 per day.
Adwave's page gives an example that a $1,000 CTV campaign at a $25 CPM delivers 40,000 impressions.
facts.quote: At $25 CPM, a $1,000 CTV campaign delivers 40,000 impressions to targeted voters.

facts.fact: Amazon Freevee CTV CPMs are listed at $18-28.
YouTube skippable video political ads are listed at $10-25 CPM.
YouTube non-skippable 15-second political video ads are listed at $15-35 CPM.
Facebook/Instagram image ads are listed at $5-15 CPM and click costs at $0.50-3.00 CPC.
facts.quote: Image ads: $5-15 CPM * Carousel: $6-18 CPM * Click cost: $0.50-3.00 CPC

facts.fact: Google Ads candidate name search terms are listed at $2-10 CPC.
Standard programmatic display political CPMs are listed at $2-8.
Major market radio 30-second drive time spots are listed at $200-800.
Small market radio 30-second drive time spots are listed at $25-150.
Political ad rates in October are listed as 100-200% above the January-June baseline.
Final two weeks before Election Day are listed at 150-300% above baseline political ad rates.
The page states a $10,000 January buy might cost $25,000-30,000 in October for comparable reach.
facts.quote: A $10,000 January buy might cost $25,000-30,000 in October.

facts.fact: Battleground states are listed as having 30-60% higher political ad rates than non-competitive markets during peak season.
facts.quote: Expect 30-60% higher rates in these states compared to non-competitive markets during peak election season.

facts.fact: Fixed-position TV ad slots are listed at a 20-50% premium.
Preemptible TV inventory is listed at a 10-30% discount.
The page lists a competitive Senate statewide race total media budget at $10-50 million.
facts.quote: **Competitive Senate race (statewide):** * Total media budget: $10-50 million

facts.fact: The page lists a competitive House race total media budget at $1-5 million.
facts.quote: **Competitive House race:** * Total media budget: $1-5 million

facts.fact: The page lists a state legislature total media budget at $50,000-500,000.
The page lists a city/municipal race total media budget at $5,000-75,000.
Larger broadcast TV commitments are listed as earning discounts of 10-25%.
facts.quote: **Commit to volume:** Larger buys earn discounts of 10-25% for major commitments.

facts.fact: Monthly or quarterly CTV commitments are listed as often earning 5-15% lower CPMs.
facts.quote: Monthly or quarterly commitments often earn 5-15% lower CPMs.

facts.fact: Traditional agencies are listed as charging 10-15% of media spend in fees.
Traditional agencies are listed as having $5,000-15,000 monthly minimums.
The page suggests starting CTV or digital tests at $500-2,000 before larger commitments.
facts.quote: **Test first:** Start with small tests ($500-2,000) to validate performance before major commitments.

facts.fact: Per the vendor, prime-time TV in major markets such as New York and LA costs about $15,000-75,000.
facts.quote: In major markets (New York, LA), expect $15,000-75,000 for prime time.

facts.fact: Per the vendor, mid-size markets run $2,000-10,000 for TV advertising.
Per the vendor, small markets can cost as little as $200-2,000 for TV advertising.
facts.quote: Small markets can be as low as $200-2,000.

facts.fact: Per the vendor, CTV/streaming offers a consistent $20-35 CPM regardless of market.
facts.quote: CTV/streaming offers a consistent $20-35 CPM regardless of market

facts.fact: Per the vendor, broadcast TV effectively runs $30-100+ CPM when accounting for reach wasted outside the district.
facts.quote: broadcast TV effectively runs $30-100+ CPM when accounting for wasted reach outside your district

facts.fact: Per the vendor, CTV campaigns can start from $30 per day, versus $5,000+ minimums for broadcast.
facts.quote: CTV campaigns can start from $30/day versus $5,000+ minimums for broadcast.

facts.fact: Per the vendor, political TV rates can rise 100-300% in the final weeks before Election Day compared with earlier in the year.
facts.quote: Rates can increase 100-300% in the final weeks before Election Day compared to earlier in the year.

facts.fact: Per the vendor's example, a $10,000 January broadcast buy might cost $25,000-30,000 in October for equivalent reach and frequency.
facts.quote: a $10,000 January buy might cost $25,000-30,000 in October for equivalent reach and frequency.

facts.fact: The lowest unit rate applies during the 45 days before a primary and the 60 days before a general election.
facts.value: 45 days before primary; 60 days before general
facts.quote: during the 45 days before a primary and the 60 days before a general election

facts.fact: PACs, Super PACs and issue groups do not get the lowest unit rate and pay regular rates.
facts.quote: PACs, Super PACs and issue groups don't get it and pay regular rates.

facts.fact: Per the vendor, local campaigns (city, county, school board) typically allocate $5,000-50,000 for TV/CTV advertising.
facts.quote: Local campaigns (city, county, school board) typically allocate $5,000-50,000 for TV/CTV advertising.

facts.fact: Per the vendor, a $5,000 CTV campaign at $25 CPM delivers 200,000 impressions.
facts.quote: At $25 CPM on CTV, a $5,000 campaign delivers 200,000 impressions

facts.fact: Per the vendor, CTV delivers 2-3x more in-district impressions per dollar than broadcast for targeted local campaigns.
facts.quote: For targeted local campaigns, CTV delivers 2-3x more in-district impressions per dollar.

facts.fact: Per the vendor, self-serve platforms eliminate agency fees, which it says save 10-20%.
facts.quote: self-serve platforms eliminate agency fees (10-20% savings)

facts.fact: Per the vendor, broadcast TV bought during lowest unit rate windows saves 30-50% versus standard rates for federal campaigns.
facts.quote: **Broadcast TV during LUR windows** - 30-50% savings vs. standard rates

facts.fact: Under 47 CFR 73.1212, every political ad on broadcast TV needs a sponsor identification stating who paid for it.
facts.quote: Every political ad on broadcast TV needs a sponsor identification that says who paid for it
